headline_marked: PM Tarique Rahman outlines [[3-R strategy to rebuild Bangladesh]] in UNGA address
headline: PM Tarique Rahman outlines 3-R strategy to rebuild Bangladesh in UNGA address
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman addressed the 81st UN General Assembly, detailing his government's vision for national recovery, restoration, and reconstruction after years of misrule. He highlighted initiatives for economic growth, social protection, and human
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman announced a "3-R strategy" – recovery, restoration, and reconstruction – to rebuild Bangladesh at the 81st UN General Assembly in New York. He stated the country is moving past a period of "fascist rule and exploitation."

Rahman emphasized Bangladesh's return to democracy, highlighting efforts to overcome enforced disappearances, killings, corruption, and money laundering. He noted the opening of new possibilities for the nation.

The government is leveraging the demographic dividend by implementing extensive programs to transform the working-age population into skilled human resources. Measures are underway to create widespread employment and develop Bangladesh as a "manufacturing hub," seeking international support.

A US$50 million allocation in the current fiscal year aims to foster young entrepreneurs, researchers, and innovators through start-up initiatives. The government is also prioritizing women's empowerment, with women at the forefront of socio-economic transformation plans.

Initiatives include expanded opportunities for cash financing for women, especially in small and medium-sized industries, and free education up to the undergraduate level. The government seeks to ensure both electoral democracy and economic democratization.

Social protection programs like the Family Card, Farmers' Card, Sports Card, and e-Health Card have been introduced to support economically disadvantaged people. The Family Card, issued to female household heads, symbolizes women's economic empowerment.

Rahman detailed the government's 31-point program, with 73% directly aligned with the UN Sustainable Development Goals' "Leave No One Behind" theme and 27% indirectly aligned. These programs aim to reduce urban-rural development disparities and promote inclusive sustainable development.

Education, health, and sports receive special importance, with the highest-ever budget allocation for education. Plans include increasing education spending to 5% of GDP within five years and developing a curriculum focused on technical and practical education.

Primary students receive free school bags, uniforms, and midday meals to boost enrollment and quality. Sports has been integrated into the curriculum to establish it as a profession, evidenced by a recent nationwide football tournament involving over two million students.

Addressing global issues, the PM noted that conflicts cause displacement, humanitarian crises, and pressure on the global economy and energy supply, contributing to inflation. He advocated for resolving conflicts through dialogue, diplomacy, and mutual cooperation based on equality and respect.

headline_marked: [[Vegetable and fish prices surge]] after fuel price hike; bottled soybean oil scarce
headline: Vegetable and fish prices surge after fuel price hike; bottled soybean oil scarce
summary: Following the recent fuel price increase, consumers in Dhaka are facing higher costs for most vegetables and fish, with some items seeing a Tk 5-20 per kg rise. Bottled soybean oil is also becoming increasingly scarce in markets.
details: Following the government's recent increase in fuel prices, consumers are experiencing a noticeable rise in the cost of vegetables and fish across Dhaka markets. The hike in diesel, petrol, and octane prices has led to increased truck rental costs, impacting prices at every stage from production to retail.

Several types of vegetables have seen price increases of Tk 5 to Tk 20 per kilogram. Eggplant, for instance, which previously sold for Tk 80-140, now costs Tk 100-160, while pointed gourd, spiny gourd, and yardlong beans have risen from Tk 80 to Tk 100-120.

Fish prices have also climbed, with increases ranging from Tk 20 to Tk 50 per kilogram. Shing fish, for example, now sells for around Tk 500 per kg, up by Tk 30-50, with similar increases observed for Koi, Pabda, Shrimp, Tilapia, Pangash, and Rui.

Beyond fresh produce, the prices of open flour and refined flour have also increased by Tk 5 and Tk 10 per kg respectively over the past month. Broiler chicken and eggs have maintained high prices for about 1.5 months, selling at Tk 180-200 per kg and Tk 150 per dozen.

Adding to consumer woes, one- and two-liter bottled soybean oil are increasingly scarce in markets, with a slight reduction in the supply of five-liter bottles. Edible oil refining companies had already raised bottled soybean oil prices by Tk 5 per liter earlier this month, bringing the price to Tk 204 per liter.

Retailers report that companies are supplying less oil to the market, with dealers indicating that companies may be seeking further price increases. However, the scarcity of bottled soybean oil is not uniform across all markets.
